qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r2/raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of workspace.cjs 773cc339... and results/workspace.json dc9925be... re-verified with sha256sum and match)
evidence: Time-varying public promises (instruction.md): other people's moves within 15 s without reload and without closing the open card, wiping the typed note or moving the cursor; message arrival while scrolled up or mid-draft keeps place/draft/cursor and gives a notice; unread/seen per person; earlier messages without losing place; drafts survive switch/reload/sign-out; refused move put back with reason. The brief explicitly excludes theme switching and phone layout, and drag is optional, so no resize/theme toggle is owed; visual/prompt.md:14 correctly says 'conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' Each time-varying promise is exercised by real actions and waits, not a first paint: functional/judge.toml hro_live_board (lines 286-291) 'without reload or click, within 15 seconds this page shows the other recruiter's move ... and the newly added card' driven by protocol V (prompt.md:47: independent context acts, 'Without reloading or clicking in this page, wait up to 15 seconds (a wait-for call, or snapshots ...)'); hro_msg_exchange (295-300), hro_unread_counts (330-336), hro_seen (348-354) and hro_unread_scrolled_up (339-345) all driven by protocol U (prompt.md:41 'Every reading in U is made without reloading, navigating or clicking in Rafael's page: wait up to 15 seconds after the other person acts'); hro_thread_latest/earlier require scrolling and repeated loading; hro_drafts requires switching and reload; hro_refused_put_back (131-138) reads document.activeElement after a refused move; hro_restart uses restart_app. Polish (polish/judge.toml) owns preservation under live updates with explicit interaction plus wait: hro_pol_live_board types an unfinished note, scrolls, has another context move a card, waits 15 s with no reload, then checks details open, exact note text, document.activeElement, scroll offset and that further typing appends (cursor not reset); hro_pol_live_thread does the same for a mid-draft reply; hro_pol_earlier_place measures getBoundingClientRect().top before/after loading earlier messages; hro_pol_failed_send aborts one request/sets offline; hro_pol_session_resume ends the session in a second tab. polish/prompt.md:14 forbids reload/navigate/click/type in the observed page until the update is seen or 15 s pass, and says page.evaluate reads are not interaction. Gates are correctly static (sign-in/shared-storage only). Golden scripted evidence (not a judge run): results/workspace.json groups 'live board ... open card, note draft and focus kept' passed with arrival_ms 806, 'conversation ... arrival while reading keeps draft, focus and scroll and is not marked read until viewed' passed, 'seen receipt and unread badges update live' passed, page_errors []. Broken-app attempts: a poll-free app that only refreshes on click fails hro_live_board/U rows (no-click rule); an app that live-updates by re-rendering the whole board fails hro_pol_live_board; an app that marks read on arrival fails hro_unread_scrolled_up. Conforming alternatives (SSE, websocket or <=15 s polling; modal or side-panel card details; drag plus buttons) are not penalised because detection is by observable outcome. Residual P3 notes (not row failures): (1) 'accept the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds' (functional prompt.md:41,47) lets a slow LLM judge whose first snapshot lands at, say, 25 s credit a ~20 s poller that misses the public 15 s promise; precise timing via browser_wait_for timeout or Date.now() stamps would tighten it, though policy discourages fine timing distinctions. (2) hro_pol_live_board's scroll leg has no instruction for a board where neither the page nor any container scrolls; the reset cannot then be observed, which favours the model rather than harming a conforming app. Risk=true only because required runtime evidence is missing: raw-evidence-index scope states full configured grading is absent, so whether the configured claude-code/glm judge actually waits, avoids clicks and reads activeElement/scroll as instructed is NOT EXERCISED; the scripted golden run is not judge evidence.
